prerequisites: Prior knowledge of Physics, Mathematics, and Mechanics is required.

learning_outcomes.text: Model a mechanism and/or machine as a discrete system, defining the fundamental parameters that characterize its vibratory behavior.
Create a vibroacoustic model of a machine.
Apply concepts of noise and vibrations in machine design.
Use numerical simulation programs suitable for dynamic analysis of mechanisms and machines, being able to analyze and discuss the obtained results.
Understand the assembly and operation of measurement chains, and acquire the skill to use them.
Prepare reports on measurements: objective, procedure, results, analysis, and recommendations.
Know the sources that generate vibrations in machines.
Calculate the actions generated by dynamic imbalances in machines.
Know the regulations that evaluate the severity of vibrations in a machine.
Apply corrective measures to minimize the transmission of noise and vibrations.

syllabus_topics: Instrumentation for noise and vibration measurement
Sources of vibrations and noise in machines
assessment_rules: For continuous assessment, a minimum grade of 4/10 is required in each section (assignment work, practices, partial tests) to average the different parts. If the minimum for practices is not reached, this part will be assessed in the global evaluation. Partial knowledge tests are voluntary; if not passed, they can be taken during official examination calls. The global evaluation, in official calls, consists of a knowledge test (30%), a practice exam (30%), and questions on assignment work activities (40%), covering previously unpassed parts.
